methodological_rigor.justification: Validation study of two open-source AI models (EAGLE, DeepGEM) on histopathology for EGFR prediction. Appropriate use of AUC, bootstrap CIs, ancestry-stratified analyses. TRIPOD-AI guideline adherence. However, generalization limited by two cohorts, EGFR prevalence differences, lack of centralized image review. Ancestry categorization limited to DFCI cohort.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Validation/diagnostic accuracy study (LoE 4) with moderate clinical relevance. AI-based EGFR prediction from histology could accelerate diagnosis (57% test reduction). However, ancestry-dependent performance (AUC 0.68 in Asian vs 0.84 in European) raises equity concerns. Utility limited until performance harmonized across populations.

reporting_quality.justification: TRIPOD-AI guideline adherence reported. Clear description of cohorts, mutation profiling methods, ancestry inference. Statistical methods comprehensive. Ancestry stratification analyses presented. Limitations acknowledged including lack of centralized review. Code/model availability not specified.

novelty_literature.justification: Validates published AI models (EAGLE, DeepGEM) in new cohorts. Identifies important finding (ancestry-associated performance variability) but this reflects known issues in medical AI. Incremental contribution identifying existing problem rather than solving it.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized with clear methods, results stratified by model and ancestry, ROC curves. Discussion appropriately addresses implications of performance variability. Figures communicate model performance effectively across subgroups. Limitations section candid about equity concerns.

key_strengths: Large multicohort validation (2,098 patients) of open-source EGFR prediction models across US and European sites
Identifies critical equity issue: EAGLE AUC 0.68 in Asian vs 0.84 in European ancestry, despite higher EGFR prevalence in Asian group
Comprehensive analyses including tissue-type performance differences (pleural samples AUC 0.66)
Dual-threshold strategy achieves 57% test reduction while maintaining 0.84 sensitivity, 0.99 specificity
TRIPOD-AI compliance and candid limitations discussion
key_concerns: Ancestry categorization limited to DFCI cohort; limited generalizability of ancestry-stratified findings
Cannot determine whether performance differences relate to morphologic variation, staining protocols, or model training limitations
Relatively small numbers in some ancestry subgroups (54 African, 95 Asian) limit statistical power
Lack of centralized image review; institutional variation in scanning/staining not controlled
Clinical implementation hampered by ancestry-dependent performance variance and lack of real-world validation data
chief_reviewer.rationale: Identifies important equity concern in AI model generalizability (ancestry-associated performance variability). Competent validation study with clinical potential but findings highlight need for population-specific model recalibration before deployment. Fits Tier 3; supports research into equitable AI development.
